title: Fourier coefficients vanish above the tree depth
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $S \subseteq \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ be a set of variables whose cardinality $\abs{S}$ exceeds the depth of $T$. Then the coefficient assigned to the frequency $S$ vanishes, $\mathrm{coeffs}\,T\,S = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n variables
S is a subset of the variable indices
depth of T is strictly less than the cardinality of S
replaced:
If $T.\mathrm{depth} < \abs{S}$, then $\mathrm{coeffs}\,T\,S = 0$: frequencies of
cardinality exceeding the tree depth carry no weight.
